question: What are we actually trying to do?
summary: Reaches shared understanding before the work starts — on planning, research, writing or code.
share: What are we actually trying to do? Reaches shared understanding with an AI before the work starts — on planning, research, writing or code.
homeBlurb: Get on the same page before the work starts.
tryOnce: Before you start, work out whether we actually understand this the same way. Use what is already in this conversation first, then sort it into what you know, what you can reasonably infer, what you could look up yourself, and what genuinely needs a decision from me. Close the first three yourself and say your inferences out loud. Ask me only about the last group, and where the answer can be reduced to choices, offer me the choices rather than an open question. Recommend what you would do. Stop as soon as we understand it well enough to move.

example.caption: A short request with a lot of unsaid context — and not a line of code in sight.

turns.text: Help me write a message to my landlord about the boiler without it sounding harsh.
Sure — here's a polite draft asking them to arrange a repair at their earliest convenience.

Before drafting: I know it's about the boiler and you don't want to sound harsh. I'm assuming it's a repeat problem rather than the first report — say if not. One thing that changes the whole message: what do you actually want out of it? (A) it fixed quickly, no friction (B) a firm record because this has dragged on (C) compensation or rent reduction. I'd guess B from "without sounding harsh". Tell me the letter and I'll write it.

usefulWhen: There is more context in your head than you have actually said out loud.
The request is short and the work it implies is large.
The work is expensive, public, or hard to undo.
notNeededWhen: The task is small, reversible and unambiguous.
The goal was established earlier in the same conversation.
Asking would cost more than trying it and adjusting.

options.label: Questioning level
options.help: How much is asked before work starts.

choices.label: Minimal
choices.line: - **Questioning level.** Ask at most one question, and only when the work cannot sensibly begin without the answer.

choices.label: Balanced
choices.line: - **Questioning level.** Ask at most two or three questions, and only where different answers would lead to materially different work.

choices.label: Thorough
choices.line: - **Questioning level.** Ask as many questions as the ambiguity warrants, covering goal, boundaries and completion conditions before starting.

options.label: Question style
options.help: Whether you get choices to pick from, or open questions.

choices.label: Offer choices
choices.line: - **Question style.** Offer a short list of options whenever the answer can sensibly be reduced to choices, and fall back to an open question only when it cannot.

choices.label: Ask openly
choices.line: - **Question style.** Ask open questions rather than offering options, so the answer is not shaped by the choices on offer.

options.label: Small tasks
options.help: Whether quick reversible work skips the check.

choices.label: Skip the check
choices.line: - **Small tasks.** Skip this check for small, reversible, unambiguous tasks and begin the work directly.

choices.label: Always run it
choices.line: - **Small tasks.** Run this check on every task, however small, but keep the output to a single line when the goal is already clear.

options.label: What survives
options.help: What is left behind when the task is finished.

choices.label: Only what must outlive it
choices.line: - **What survives.** Keep the working understanding in the conversation. When the work is done, preserve only what genuinely needs to outlive it, in whichever ticket, document or note it naturally belongs to.

choices.label: Always write it down
choices.line: - **What survives.** Write a short goal-and-boundaries summary before starting and keep it as a durable artefact alongside the work.

choices.label: Leave nothing
choices.line: - **What survives.** Keep everything in the conversation and preserve nothing once the work is done.
